problem_text:
A city planner needs to allocate a fixed budget across 10 infrastructure projects to maximize the overall community benefit score.  
The characteristics of each project are as follows:  
* Project A: benefit score 0.155, environmental impact 0.123, allocation limits [0.094, 0.480]  
* Project B: benefit score 0.194, environmental impact 0.234, allocation limits [0.014, 0.786]  
* Project C: benefit score 0.097, environmental impact 0.181, allocation limits [0.031, 0.369]  
* Project D: benefit score 0.022, environmental impact 0.155, allocation limits [0.046, 0.810]  
* Project E: benefit score 0.067, environmental impact 0.110, allocation limits [0.021, 0.689]  
* Project F: benefit score 0.112, environmental impact 0.017, allocation limits [0.048, 0.706]  
* Project G: benefit score 0.113, environmental impact 0.040, allocation limits [0.048, 0.399]  
* Project H: benefit score 0.124, environmental impact 0.131, allocation limits [0.044, 0.890]  
* Project I: benefit score 0.124, environmental impact 0.289, allocation limits [0.070, 0.446]  
* Project J: benefit score 0.100, environmental impact 0.044, allocation limits [0.032, 0.405]  

Each project must receive a budget share within its specified limits, and the total allocation across all projects must sum to one. To prioritize quick implementation, the set of rapid-delivery projects L = {A, G, H, I} must collectively receive at least 0.482 of the total budget. Additionally, the total environmental impact of all selected projects must not exceed 0.168, and the overall community benefit score must be at least 0.074.  

Determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes the total community benefit while satisfying all constraints.
